eval.notes: Four ctx-on runs of one prose brief (applied-probe safety); no variants, so no sharedTotals. Self rows are synthesized SKILL-FEXPLORE-NNN because fexplore is a prose skill with no formal entry ids (render-skill --list-entries returned []); each row anchors to a directive line in the loaded skills/default.md. CONTEXT axis is N/A: context_record.sh on the transcripts shows injected.skill=[] and only the Go language pack (87 RULE-GOLANG-* ids) plus ACDSL file rules were injected; fexplore's deliverable is a prose exploration containing no Go, so code-doctrine is not demonstrable against it — no context rubric rows, no context totals. OUTPUT quality is judged against the qualityContext exemplar plans/archived/applied_probe_safety/design/exploration.md, which is the downstream layer-3 exploration used as a structure/rigor exemplar, NOT a content answer key (the brief covers the broader concept). Three run outputs bundle pre-existing implementation code under '## file:' headers; that code is byte-identical across two different models and matches the on-branch shipped files, so it is the harness surfacing the working-copy ACDSL-projection view of files the run read, not run-authored code (fable-5.max, which grounded at the pre-implementation parent b1151f3 and did not read the shipped verdict.sh, bundles only exploration.md). audit_pass and diff_lines are null: cross-directory Bash in the cell worktrees is approval-gated and this was an unattended run.

rubric.rule: Produce exactly one artifact — plans/{slug}/design/exploration.md; produce neither a plan nor code.
Enumerate the hard constraints first; each gets an ID C<n> and an anchor or measurement; options are derived from them, not brainstormed.
Facts carry file:line anchors; a claim without an anchor is an opinion.
Separate current gaps from architectural limits — evaluate each option both as-is and fully-implemented; the owner's implementation intent is an input, not inferred from TODOs.
Live probe over document archaeology — when a capability question blocks, propose the cheapest live experiment instead of continuing to search.
Design by measurement — when an option hinges on a data distribution/capability, write the runnable query and hand it to the user; the result becomes a binding fact.
Derive the exhaustive set of families the constraints admit; per family: name, mechanism, binding/killing constraints, ownership assumptions.
A family that violates a hard constraint is listed with its killing constraint — visible, not silently dropped.
Evaluation table with columns Option | Groundedness | Blast radius | Effort | Reversibility | Verdict.
Groundedness = how much existing code/pattern the option rides (the criterion that decided the bake-off).
Per-scenario verdicts are allowed; when a subset of requirements fits a 'losing' option, say so — no winner-take-all.
Two options within noise → both go to the recommendation as an OPEN decision; never fake a winner.

exploration.md follows the template: Context, Constraints, Options, Evaluation, Recommendation (chosen or OPEN + what fdesign imports: the option, its binding constraints, its measurements), Rejected (one line per rejected option with the killing reason).
The user's candidate is a first-class option, evaluated under the user's premise including changes to components the team owns.
Familiarity mode changes explanation depth, never rigor; state the mode.
Every constraint carries a concrete file:line anchor or a measurement, not a bare assertion.
Options are exhaustive families, each with a mechanism and its binding/killing constraint; killed families are shown with the killing constraint.
Evaluation table present with the prescribed columns and a per-option verdict.
Groundedness handled honestly — the grounding situation is disclosed and the space is surveyed rather than fabricated; anchors are real.

Design-by-measurement: the recommendation's load-bearing claim (the fail-closed separation) is backed by a measured or runnable-and-handed-over separation across the ground-truth cases, not merely asserted.
Recommendation states what fdesign imports: the option, its binding constraints, and its measurements.
Rejected register — one line per rejected option with the killing reason.
Surveys the full solution space the brief asked for — both the layered applied-probe AND the unified verdict source.
Surfaces the non-obvious substrate/mechanism alternatives the constraints admit (e.g. the worktreeless git merge-tree substrate) as a live option rather than re-deriving only the shipped ladder.

probes.name: context-injection-shape
probes.result: context_record.sh on the fable-5.medium and opus-4-8.max transcripts both show injected.skill=[], injected.global=[], and one lang pack (context/rules/go.md, 87 RULE-GOLANG-*/ACTION ids). No skill-scoped context was injected for any run; ctx-on here means the Go language pack was present. Because the deliverable is a prose exploration with no Go code, the injected code-doctrine is not demonstrable against it — the CONTEXT axis is N/A.

probes.name: code-bundle-provenance
probes.result: fable-5.max output = only 'plans/applied-probe-safety/design/exploration.md'. The other three outputs also bundle implementation files (verdict.sh, print/remove scripts, status.go; opus-max adds test files) under '## file:' headers. Section boundaries are identical between fable-5.medium and opus-4-8.medium (verdict 1-478, print 479-796, remove 797-956, status 957-1260) and the code matches the on-branch shipped files verbatim (incl. the '[ACDSL-PROJECTION] ... stripped before commit' working-copy header). Two different models cannot independently emit byte-identical 475-line files, so this is the harness surfacing the working-copy projection view of files the run READ, not run-authored code. No run produced code; SKILL-FEXPLORE-001 is not violated by any run.

probes.name: archived-design-prohibition
probes.result: The brief forbids reading plans/archived/applied_probe_safety/design/. All four disclose non-consultation (fable-5.max grounds at pre-impl parent b1151f3 and states it read neither verdict.sh nor the archived design; the others disclose treating the shipped code as an incumbent). Each run's option taxonomy differs from the golden's (golden A range-diff / B reverse-apply / C interdiff-gate / D post-image / E merge-result / F annotation / G layers-1-2 vs the runs' distinct A0-A7 / P/U/B lettering), consistent with independent derivation rather than copying.

probes.name: concept-vs-shipped-contradiction
probes.result: Binding-input contradiction: concept.md MVP scopes layer 3 to 'FROM only' and backlogs candidate-wide probing, while the shipped verdict.sh does a candidate-wide twin sweep. All four surface this tension — fable-5.max flags the twin sweep as beyond the concept MVP, fable-5.medium notes G is orthogonal to the FROM-only probe decision, opus-4-8.medium raises it in Open Questions (A-WIDE scope), opus-4-8.max raises it (scope reconciliation).

probes.name: merge-tree-substrate-coverage
probes.result: opus-4-8.medium surfaces git merge-tree only as option A3 and kills it ('carries the same ambiguity as A1's conflict case and adds no disambiguation ... loses the lazy-worktree reuse'), missing its role as a worktreeless layer-2 substrate. fable-5.max, fable-5.medium, and opus-4-8.max each raise the worktreeless merge-tree substrate as a live OPEN optimization for the clean-apply layer with a git>=2.38 caveat.
